To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

when a self-sustaining gas discharge was excited in the gasdynamic chamber of a CO2 laser with an unstable resonator, the resonator began to operate in a self- oscillatory regime and the acoustic wave generated in the gasdynamic laser channel was responsible for generating the characteristic electromagnetic radiation emitted from the gas discharge chamber at frequencies that were governed by the Dopler effect.
the operation of an unstable laser resonator in a self- oscillatory mode is governed by the Dopplereffect.

acoustic waves are generated in the gasdynamic channels of CO2 lasers utilizing a self-sustain discharge when the input energy is low, and these acoustic waves generate electromagnetic radiation at frequencies governed by Doppler effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the physical processes governing the operation of an unstable CO2 laser resonator utilizing a self-sustainable gas-discharge channel.
the investigation of the relationship between the self-ocillatory operation of a CO2 laser with an unstable resonator and the electrical parameters in the discharge channel.
the study of the effect of the gas-dischare chamber electrical parameters on the self-oscillation of the unstable resonator of the fast-flow CO2 gas laser.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the self-oscillation of the unstable resonator was the result of a self-oscillation process in the gas-discharge system, and the acoustic waves were the result of self-oscillations in the unstable resonator.

the self-oscillation of a fast-flow laser with an unstable resonator is caused by the acoustic oscillations of the gasdynamic channel, which, in turn, are generated by the self-sustained gas discharge.

the self-oscillation regime of the resonator is the result of the self-sustained gas-discharge operation and the acoustic waves in the gasdynamic flow are the result of self-oscillating unstable resonator operation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a fast-flow CO\({}_{2}\) laser utilizing a self- sustained discharge and an unstable resonator operated as a self-oscillation generator.
the unstable resonators of a fast-flow laser can be used for the detection of acoustic waves in the gasdynamic flow channel of the laser.
a resonator with an unstable output mirror and an input mirror with a small aperture can be operated in a selfoscillatory regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the self-oscillation of an unstable resonators is a consequence of the self-sustained operation of the gas discharge in the laser.
the acoustic waves generated in the gasdynamic channels of the laser were responsible for the generation of the electromagnetic radiation at the frequencies of the Doppler effect.
the unstable resonators of CO2 lasers operating with a self-sustaining discharge may be used as sensors for the detection of acoustic waves.
